subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Support Plan Trap
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Support Plan Trap.

hook.text: AWS Enterprise Support costs $15,000/month minimum — or 3% of your bill, whichever is higher.

buildup.text: Cloud support tiers range from free (community forums only) to enterprise (24/7 phone with 15-minute response).

discovery.text: Business-critical outages without premium support mean waiting days. With it, you get help in minutes.

twist.text: Many companies buy premium support after a crisis and keep paying even when they rarely use it.

climax.text: Support costs are percentage-based. As your cloud bill grows, so does the support fee — automatically.

punchline.text: Free support is slow. Premium support is expensive. Choose wisely.

quiz.question: Why does cloud support become more expensive over time?
options: Premium tiers charge a percentage of your bill, so costs grow with usage
Cloud providers increase support prices every year
Support plans require a minimum three-year commitment

details.summary: Cloud support plans can cost 3 to 10 percent of your total monthly bill. Enterprise support from AWS costs at least $15,000 per month. While essential for production workloads, many organizations pay for premium support across all accounts when only production needs it.
details.whyItMatters: Support costs are often overlooked in cloud budgets but they add a significant percentage on top of the base bill. Matching the support level to the account's criticality saves money.
takeaways: Enterprise support costs 3 to 10 percent of total cloud spend
Only production accounts may need premium support levels
Dev and test accounts can use free or basic support tiers

faq.question: What do premium support plans include?
faq.answer: Enterprise plans typically include 24/7 access to senior engineers, 15-minute response times for critical issues, a dedicated technical account manager, architecture reviews, and proactive monitoring. Business plans offer similar coverage with slower response times.

faq.question: How should you allocate support plans across accounts?
faq.answer: Apply enterprise or business support only to production accounts. Use developer or basic support for development, staging, and sandbox accounts. This can reduce total support costs by 50 percent or more while maintaining full coverage where it matters.
